title: Fireflies
suits: products about attention, sleep, calm, nature, community or small signals adding up (a sync, a swarm, a network that lights up together). Not for loud, fast or enterprise pitches.

params.data-tod: 0…1, the hour: 0 late dusk (apricot afterglow, peach moon rising in the clearing), 0.5 blue hour, 1 moonlit night with shafts
params.data-seed: integer; reshuffles the trees and the flies (keep one seed across a deck so it stays one place)
params.data-print-t: clock time of the still frame for print (default 69: the deer is mid-clearing, grazing)
params.--ff-glow: firefly colour as #rrggbb on .sc-fireflies (default #ceff68); a brand accent works
params.--brand on the section: optional: the bioluminescent mushrooms at the foot of the big trunk take --brand (default cyan)

details: fireflies flash on a J-curve like the real ones: on in 0.14 s, a slower 0.4 s fade
a third flash in loose synchrony: every 13 s a burst of four flashes ripples left to right across the glade, each fly a little early or late
a fifth are glowers that hold a slow two-second glow instead of flashing
one firefly has landed on a fern by the big trunk and glows low and slow
flies that drift right past the eye are big out-of-focus discs
the count follows the hour: a few at dusk, about 120 by full night
a deer crosses the far clearing every 97 s: it stops to graze, lifts its head to look toward you, flags its white tail and walks on behind the bushes
the deer casts a faint shadow and grass grows in front of its hooves, so it stands in the meadow instead of floating
the owl blinks every few seconds with its right eye a beat behind; one blink in five is slow and sleepy
every 37 s the owl swivels its head away and back; its eyes glow amber only once it is dark
a bat zigzags across the upper right, at dusk only
the moon rises out of the clearing at dusk (large and peach) and stands high and white by night; stars near it are drowned out
at night moonlight shafts fan from the moon and breathe slowly; dust motes drift only inside the shafts
two fog banks drift at different speeds (300 s and 140 s a loop) between the tree rows
bioluminescent mushrooms glow at the foot of the big trunk once it is dark
the rim light changes sides: warm from the western afterglow at dusk, silver from the moon at night
two far rows of trees fade toward the sky colour; through the clearing you see the furthest trees in mist
faint bark lines run down the moonlit side of the big trunk
film grain and a tinted vignette, never pure black
